transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Jordan Blake, Maya Chen, Luis Ortega (Redwood) / Tom Rivera, Priya Singh, Ethan Park, Sara Lim (Oakridge)

Summary: quick POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload profile, and benchmark plan for Oakridge's LLM-powered customer support and fraud-detection features.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Blake from Redwood, AE on this account, with Maya and Luis from our infra team. how's everyone?
[00:06] Tom: Good thanks, Tom here. we wanted to dig into the POC scope - specifically, can you help us model our traffic and run benchmarks that reflect our real workload.
[00:15] Jordan: Absolutely, that's the plan. quick agenda: gather QPS/concurrency, token lengths, success criteria (latency/cost/quality), and agree on artifacts and timeline.
[00:28] Priya: I'll start with context — we're a mid-size fintech processing customer messages and a nightly rerank job. Real-time chat is the critical path, we need p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts. batch reranking can be async up to a few seconds.
[00:45] Maya: ok, when you say short prompts, what's the typical token distribution? avg input tokens? avg and tail for outputs?
[00:54] Priya: avg input ~120 tokens, output avg ~60 tokens, but for some investigative flows output can be 300-500 tokens (5-10% of requests). Most requests are text-gen for support replies; ~20% are embedding calls for search/rerank.
[01:15] Luis: got it. any estimate on peak QPS and concurrency?
[01:20] Tom: baseline QPS around 30 qps, peak around 150 qps during batch window or promo spikes. concurrent active sessions roughly 50-70.
[01:30] Sara: for the fraud workflows, we do synchronous inference in our payment path so we need low tail latency; we prioritize p95 for those calls.
[01:40] Jordan: good, this helps. typical PoC we run a benchmark that mirrors your mix: ~70% short chat-gen, 20% embeddings, 10% long-gen/rerank. we'll seed the benchmark with those token distributions.
[01:55] Priya: question on deployment options — we're leaning towards Dedicated but want to see hosted first. network policy is strict, we require VPC peering and customer-managed keys for Private.
[02:08] Maya: yep we support hosted + dedicated + private. for Dedicated we can provision reserved GPU pool. for SOC2/compliance we send our security pack.
[02:18] Ethan: cost is a big factor. show us unit economics — tokens per dollar for different configs, e.g., A100 quantized vs fully FP16 on H100 if available.
[02:30] Luis: we'll include quantization profiles and expected throughput per GPU type in the benchmark report. also note caching opportunities — prefix and KV cache for repeated prompts can cut token cost by ~20-40% depending on reuse.
[02:45] Tom: how do you handle fallbacks when Dedicated capacity is maxed? we need graceful degradation for high-traffic windows.
[02:53] Jordan: smart routing: requests can failover to hosted or lower-cost model variants; we'll configure routing policy for latency-critical paths to prefer Dedicated and fallback to hosted.
[03:05] Priya: also curious about batching effects on latency. our synchronous path can't wait for batching that adds 200ms; what's the tuning levers?
[03:15] Maya: we tune batching by max batch delay and priority queues. for latency-critical endpoints we set low max delay and smaller batch sizes; for throughput tasks we allow bigger batch windows. we'll test a few profiles in the PoC.
[03:30] Tom: can you give a rough estimate: for 150 QPS with avg tokens 180 (in+out), what's p95 on a Dedicated pool?
[03:40] Maya: rough back-of-envelope: on a well-tuned A100 pool with prefix cache and optimized kernels, p95 for short prompts could be under 300-400ms, but it depends on model family and sequence length. with quantized LLMs and KV caching it'll be better. we'll quantify in the benchmark.
[03:57] Priya: we also need to test our rerank batch — about 2k items per job, runs nightly, tolerates up to 30s latency but needs throughput.
[04:06] Luis: for rerank and embeddings we'll size separate worker pools or async job runners. we'll model that in the workload mix so the benchmark covers both sync and async flows.
[04:20] Jordan: success criteria — let's define them now. propose: 1) p95 latency for sync chat <= 300ms on PoC config, 2) model output quality at parity with current baseline (we'll share evaluation prompts), 3) unit cost metrics: tokens per dollar within your target (you said <$8 per 1M tokens equivalent?) and 4) secure deployment with VPC and audit logs.
[04:40] Tom: cost target is $7-9 per 1M tokens, yes. quality — we have a 500-prompt eval set for customer replies, we'll share.
[04:50] Priya: timeline — can we run a 24-hour benchmark in the next week? we have capacity to provide sample traces tomorrow.
[04:58] Jordan: yes we can. Maya, Luis, can you run a 24-hour synthetic run based on the traces and push results?
[05:04] Maya: yes, we'll provision a benchmark cluster, run the mixed workload, capture p50/p95/p99, token counts, and cost estimates. we'll also test a canary with Dedicated -> hosted fallback.
[05:18] Ethan: for the security pack, we need KMS integration details and DPA clause — legal will review.
[05:24] Jordan: we'll send SOC2, ISO, and KMS integration docs and a network diagram.
[05:30] Tom: a few clarifying items — our traffic has a peaky diurnal pattern and occasional promo spikes that double QPS for 10-20 minutes, so the benchmark should include spike tests.
[05:45] Luis: we'll include spike scenarios: baseline -> 2x -> 3x for short windows and capture degradation behavior.
[05:52] Priya: for token distribution, I'll attach histograms: median input 110, 75th 200, 95th 420; output median 55, 95th 380.
[06:05] Maya: perfect — that tail will inform model choice and batching knobs. also we'll look at KV cache hit rates; if you have many repeated prefixes that helps latency and cost.
[06:18] Jordan: on benchmarks we'll provide per-route dashboards: tokens, latency buckets, GPU utilization, and cost estimate. we'll include a raw CSV and a summary deck.
[06:30] Tom: how long to spin up Dedicated trial?
[06:34] Jordan: usually 3-5 business days to provision a reserved pool depending on approvals; for the PoC we can run on hosted capacity first while provisioning Dedicated in parallel.
[06:45] Sara: do you support customer-managed keys?
[06:47] Jordan: yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM and for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS for data-at-rest encryption. we'll detail in the security pack.
[06:58] Ethan: ok, if Redwood can demonstrate p95 < 300ms for our short chat mix and stay within cost target, we're open to a 3-month pilot with reserved capacity.
[07:08] Jordan: that's great — we'll aim for that.
[07:12] Priya: anything else on monitoring? we want per-route traces and token-level cost breakdowns.
[07:18] Luis: Redwood Console will show per-route cost and latency, and we can add tracing hooks to your observability stack.
[07:25] Tom: one more question — fallback model variants: can we run a smaller quantized model for non-critical paths?
[07:31] Maya: yes, routing policies can fall back to smaller quantized variants; we can measure quality/regression on your eval set.
[07:40] Jordan: OK let's recap action items and timeline now.
[07:44] Jordan: Oakridge to provide traces + eval prompts by 2027-03-16; Redwood to provision benchmark and run 24-hr test with spike scenarios and submit report by 2027-03-19; Redwood to send pricing and security docs by 2027-03-17; schedule 2-hr bench review the week of 2027-03-22.
[07:58] Tom: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:01] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links (security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security/oakridge-pack, benchmark template: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/template).
[08:12] End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional label swaps and small word errors (e.g., "KV cash" vs "KV cache"). The transcript aligns with a ~55 minute scoping call and includes the key QPS/concurrency numbers and token distributions discussed above.
